Change c0339. Location: 1818 Vol. III, Ch. I; 1831 Ch. XVIII.

Context before (unchanged): You, perhaps, regard her as your sister, without any wish that she might become your wife.

1818 text: Nay, you may have met with another whom you may love; and, considering yourself as bound in honour to your cousin, this struggle may occasion the poignant misery which you appear to feel." "My dear father, re-assure yourself.

1831 text: Nay, you may have met with another whom you may love; and, considering yourself as bound in honour to Elizabeth, this struggle may occasion the poignant misery which you appear to feel." "My dear father, reassure yourself.

Diff: Nay, you may have met with another whom you may love; and, considering yourself as bound in honour to [-your cousin-] {+Elizabeth+} , this struggle may occasion the poignant misery which you appear to feel. " " My dear father, [-re-assure-] {+reassure+} yourself.

Context after (unchanged): I love my cousin tenderly and sincerely.

result.rationale: Replacing "your cousin" with the name "Elizabeth" makes the bond explicit and personal, shifting how Elizabeth's relation to Victor reads; the "re-assure" to "reassure" change is orthographic.
